title: High second Chern number induced by long-range hopping in a four-dimensional Dirac model
authors: Zheng-Rong Liu, Xiang Liu, Rui Chen, Bin Zhou
abstract: Four-dimensional (4D) topological systems provide a promising platform for exploring topological phenomena beyond three dimensions. So far, extensive recent studies on 4D topological insulators have focused on the 4D Dirac model, while its second Chern number is restricted to a limited set of values. In this work, we demonstrate that introducing long-range hopping into the 4D Dirac model induces topological phases with high second Chern numbers. Furthermore, we show that the long-range hopping can transform a trivial insulator into a topological insulator with a nonzero second Chern number. Our work establishes long-range hopping as a powerful route for engineering 4D topological states and reveals new possibilities for realizing unconventional topological phases beyond minimal models.
summary: This paper investigates how incorporating long-range hopping into the 4D Dirac model can generate novel topological phases. The authors demonstrate that this mechanism allows for the creation of insulating states with high second Chern numbers ($C_2$), values unattainable in simpler models. This establishes long-range interactions as a powerful tool for engineering advanced topological matter.
main_problem: To determine if introducing long-range hopping into the four-dimensional (4D) Dirac model can induce topological phases characterized by high second Chern numbers ($C_2$), thereby expanding beyond the limitations of minimal models.
main_result: Long-range hopping is shown to be a powerful mechanism capable of inducing 4D topological insulators with significantly high and tunable second Chern numbers (e.g., $C_2=-6$ or $C_2=4$).
method: The authors calculated the second Chern number ($C_2$) using integrals involving the non-Abelian Berry curvature over the Brillouin zone, analyzing the energy spectrum under open boundary conditions to confirm bulk-boundary correspondence.
model_or_system: The study focuses on a four-dimensional (4D) Dirac model Hamiltonian extended by next-nearest-neighbor ($	ext{t}_{	ext{NNN}}$) and next-next-nearest-neighbor ($	ext{t}_{	ext{NNNN}}$) hopping terms. The system's topology is mapped in the parameter space defined by these long-range hopping amplitudes.
key_observables: Second Chern number ($C_2$), bulk energy gap ($E_g$), and the count of gapless boundary modes (verifying bulk-boundary correspondence).
important_parameters: Hopping amplitudes ($	ext{t}_1, 	ext{t}_2$) and the lattice dimension $m$ used in the model.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on diagonalizing the extended 4D Dirac Hamiltonian and using advanced numerical techniques like adaptive mesh refinement for accurate topological invariant calculation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of the bulk energy gap ($E_g$) and the second Chern number ($C_2$) as hopping parameters are varied, showing clear transitions between trivial ($C_2=0$) and highly topological phases (e.g., $C_2=-6$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework for 4D topological insulators using the Dirac model; it then systematically introduces long-range hopping terms to modify the Hamiltonian; finally, it calculates $C_2$ and demonstrates that these additions enable the realization of novel, high-$|C_2|$ phases.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete theoretical pathway—modifying lattice interactions via long-range hoppings—to engineer exotic topological states in higher dimensions, which is highly relevant for designing artificial quantum materials and superconducting circuits.
